simple.meaning: שִׁקּוּץ (shiqqûwts) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “disgusting , i.e. filthy ; especially idolatrous or (concretely) an idol.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 28 times across Deuteronomy, 1 Kings, 2 Kings, 2 Chronicles, Isaiah, and 6 more, beginning at Deuteronomy 29:16. Its contexts include altar, Torah, kingship, priesthood, prophetic witness, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שִׁקּוּץ (H8251).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: שִׁקּוּץ (shiqqûwts) / H8251 is traced through Deuteronomy 29:16, 1 Kings 11:5, 1 Kings 11:7, 2 Kings 23:13 as a generated source-based concept entry.
